session.title: The Hollow Bell, first sitting
session.note: Invented. Nobody's speech is in this file. It exists so the correction loop can be demonstrated end to end without a model, and it plants the two decisions docs/UX.md names as worth a person's attention: which spelling of a name is right, and whether two names are one thing. The wrong spelling is planted twice so a carry-forward into r0_correction_session_2.json is observable rather than asserted.

turns.text: The bell tower has been silent for eleven years, and tonight it rings twice.
We go and look. Who is still awake in the lower town at this hour?
A chandler called Vesh Kalder is still working. He waves you inside without being asked.
Vesh Calder says the bell was rung from underneath, not from the tower stair.
Underneath means the crypt. Does anyone hold a key to the crypt these days?
The Tallow Warden keeps it. He has kept it since the fire, and he answers to nobody in the town.
Ormunt still has that key? I thought the council took it off him after the fire.
They tried. Ormunt kept it anyway, and the council has not asked twice.
Fine. We pay the crypt toll if it comes to that, and we argue about it afterwards.
Somebody go and get the good lantern before we do anything else, please.

expected_analysis.summary: A bell silent for eleven years rings twice at night. A chandler in the lower town tells the party it was rung from beneath the tower, which points at the crypt, and the crypt key is held by a man the town has stopped arguing with.

scenes.title: The bell rings twice
scenes.summary: The party hears the tower bell and decides to go down into the lower town.

scenes.title: The chandler's account
scenes.summary: A chandler still working at night says the bell was rung from underneath the tower.

scenes.title: Who holds the crypt key
scenes.summary: The party works out that the crypt key never went back to the council.

entities.name: the crypt under the bell tower

threads.description: Who rang the bell from beneath the tower, and why now.
The party has agreed in principle to pay a crypt toll it has not seen the price of.

review_questions.issue: Two names may be the same person: 'the Tallow Warden' and 'Ormunt'.
review_questions.recommendation: Treat them as one character, canonically 'the Tallow Warden'.
review_questions.why_it_matters: He holds the only crypt key, so a split record would lose track of who the party has to deal with.

review_questions.issue: The chandler's surname was heard two ways: 'Vesh Kalder' and 'Vesh Calder'.
review_questions.why_it_matters: He is the party's only witness to how the bell was rung, and the spelling will become a campaign entity.

review_questions.issue: It is unclear whether the party has committed to paying the crypt toll or only to arguing about it later.
review_questions.why_it_matters: An accepted obligation and a postponed one lead to different next sessions.

review_questions.issue: It is unclear who was asked to fetch the lantern.
review_questions.why_it_matters: It may be a small character beat about who runs errands for the party.
